split_question: Should your local police be run by a named Commander for your council area, answerable to local people and elected officials?
angles: bigger regional forces with local teams inside
local people hold the power: elected or directly accountable police chief for each area
facts_for_writers: The Home Office announced around 200 Local Police Commands on 18 November 2026, each with a named Commander accountable to the local community and elected officials, covering burglary, vehicle theft, phone theft and antisocial behaviour. [s1]
The announcement gives no cost, no exact officer number and no timetable; it says thousands of officers would be freed for neighbourhood policing. [s1]
Scotland combined eight forces in 2013; the Scottish Police Authority says this saves £200 million a year and 2.5 million officer hours. [s2]
Sir Stephen Watson of Greater Manchester Police says mergers need 'a couple of billion quid' to get started; forces raise different amounts from the police precept on council tax. [s2]
In 2006 Home Secretary Charles Clarke proposed 12 to 15 larger forces; the plan was dropped after opposition from some police authorities and chief constables. [s2]

extra_sources.title: Would you support or oppose the creation of a national police service (daily question, 5,367 GB adults)

note: Poll not used as the issue's poll: YouGov 26 Jan 2026 found 71% support (30% strongly, 41% somewhat) and 10% oppose a national police service, but that is a different question from local commands and is over a month older than the news. No exact poll on local commands found.
